sources.entry: SSHFire - Cross-platform SSH client with a terminal, a session manager and an SFTP browser that follows the current directory. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/aralozaltin/sshfire) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: SSHFire is a desktop SSH client (built with Tauri, React and xterm.js on a Rust core) that combines saved servers, tabbed terminals, an SFTP file panel that follows the shell's directory, and live server metrics.
summary.what_it_does: It provides a saved server list with folders and search, plus quick connect via user@host:port. Authentication supports passwords, key files (including passphrase-protected keys), SSH agent and keyboard-interactive two-factor, with jump hosts and trust-on-first-use host key checking. Passwords and passphrases are stored in the OS key store rather than files. The terminal area offers tabs, side-by-side, stacked and grid layouts, MultiExec, macros, search, and color schemes. A metrics bar shows CPU, memory, disk, load, uptime and network (Linux servers). The SFTP panel follows the shell's working directory on Linux and macOS servers and supports copy/paste, drag-and-drop, a built-in remote text editor, and permission changes. Local, SOCKS5 and remote port forwarding are also included.
use_cases: manage multiple SSH servers in one app
browse and transfer remote files over SFTP
connect through a bastion or jump host
run multi-server commands in parallel terminals
set up SSH port forwarding tunnels
monitor remote server CPU and memory
how_to_run: npm run tauri dev # run in development
npm run tauri build # production bundle
notable: Passwords and key passphrases stored in the OS key store (Keychain, Windows Credential Manager, Linux Secret Service), never in files
SFTP panel that follows the shell's working directory
MultiExec: type once and send input to several tabs
Local, SOCKS5 dynamic and remote port forwarding saved per server
caveats: Directory-following SFTP works only with Linux and macOS servers; live network metrics are for Linux servers
Windows SmartScreen and macOS Gatekeeper may need manual confirmation on first launch, since builds are not signed in the README
Full test suite requires a Docker-based OpenSSH container and manual OS key store tests
